description: Hard questions of faith and heart: why there is suffering, trusting Allah's plan, doubts, feeling like a hypocrite, worry, fear, and finding peace.

text.en: Suffering is one of the hardest questions, and the answer is not simple. The Qur'an says life is a test, that Allah will try people with fear, hunger and loss, and that the patient are given glad tidings. The Prophet said that no tiredness, illness, worry or sorrow touches a believer without Allah wiping away some of their sins for it. Your pain is real, it is not hidden from Allah, and it is not wasted.

triggers: why does allah let bad things happen
why did this happen to me
doNotSay: Do not say suffering is deserved or a punishment. Be gentle; if grief or despair is heavy, the support path comes first.

text.en: Trusting Allah's plan means doing your part and calming your heart about the rest. You may dislike something that is good for you and love something that is bad, and Allah knows while you do not. Make dua for what you want, keep working, and when a door closes, ask for what is better. Allah is enough for the one who relies on Him.

triggers: why did allah take this from me
how do i accept what happened

text.en: Doubts come to everyone, and having them is not disbelief. When such thoughts arise, the Prophet taught to say that you believe in Allah and stop dwelling on them. Ask your questions openly, read the answers, and speak with someone who knows. Do not let a thought you dislike convince you that you have lost your faith.

triggers: i am not sure i believe
doNotSay: Never call the person a disbeliever. If the thoughts are intrusive and distressing, point to the waswas support area.

text.en: Feeling like a hypocrite worries only people who care about sincerity. The Companion Hanzala felt the same when his heart changed between the Prophet's gathering and home life, and the Prophet told him that if you were always as you are with me, the angels would shake your hand, but it is an hour and an hour. Hearts rise and fall. Keep doing the good, stay with good people, and ask Allah to keep your heart firm.

triggers: my iman goes up and down
my faith goes up and down

text.en: When you are worried or sad, say the Prophet's dua: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief. Then do one small thing that is in your hands, speak to someone you trust, and rest. Remembering Allah brings the heart rest. If the worry is heavy or does not lift, speak to a doctor or counsellor too; that is also a means Allah gave you.

triggers: what should i say when i am worried
i am worried all the time
doNotSay: If the person describes panic, hopelessness or self-harm, use the support path, not this answer.

text.en: A broken relationship hurts, and you are allowed to grieve it. Do not rush yourself. Make wudu and pray, ask Allah to take away the pain and replace it with what is better, limit contact and what keeps the wound open, and lean on family or friends you trust. Allah says you may dislike something that is good for you, and that with hardship there is ease.

triggers: how to move on from someone
how to heal a broken heart
doNotSay: Gentle. If the person is in despair or says they cannot go on, the support path comes first.

text.en: It is allowed to hurt, and it is allowed to still hurt after you have understood the reasons. Grief and faith can sit together. The Prophet wept when his son Ibrahim died and said the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. Yaqub said he complains of his sorrow only to Allah. Pour it out to Allah in your own words, let people near you share it, and give yourself time.

triggers: it still hurts even though i know
doNotSay: Never say faith should remove the pain. If grief is heavy or they cannot function, point to the grief support area.

text.en: To overcome fear, name it, do what you can about it, then place the rest with Allah. Say that Allah is enough for us and the best of guardians; this is what the believers said when people told them to fear, and it increased their faith. Fear shrinks when you act on it a step at a time and do not face it alone.

triggers: i am afraid of the future

text.en: Peace comes from remembering Allah, doing good, and accepting what you cannot change. Allah says hearts find rest in His remembrance, and that whoever does good as a believer, He gives a good life. Pray on time, keep a few minutes of quiet remembrance, be thankful for one thing at the end of each day, and give something to someone.

triggers: i want peace in my heart
doNotSay: If low mood has lasted and affects daily life, mention that a doctor or counsellor can help; do not diagnose.

text.en: Signs that Allah loves a person are not a checklist, but the Qur'an gives the path: Allah says that if you love Him, follow the Prophet and Allah will love you, and He says He loves those who do good and those who turn back to Him. Doing the obligatory well, adding voluntary prayer and remembrance, and being kind to people are the way. If you want closeness, that wish is itself a good sign.

triggers: how to make allah love me
how do i know allah loves me
how to be beloved to allah

text.en: Dua works best when you ask with presence and certainty. Begin by praising Allah and sending blessings on the Prophet, ask for what you need in plain words, ask with firm hope, and repeat it. Choose good times: the last third of the night, between adhan and iqamah, and while prostrating. Ask for both this life and the next, and keep asking.

triggers: how to make my dua accepted

text.en: The best dhikr is the one you will keep. Start with a few: say subhan Allah, alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar after each prayer, and ask forgiveness often. The Prophet said two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale and beloved to the Merciful: subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, subhan Allah al-Azim. Pair it with something you already do each day.
